FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66
DESCRIPTION: FIND — evaluate_fix() does not actually test fixes in a project sandbox. In bench/endocrine.py, it writes only the single patched file into a temp dir (`patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`) and then runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that isolated file plus optional tests with `cwd=tmpdir`. This breaks imports and package-relative context for most real files, so post-fix diagnostics and tests are evaluated in a different environment than the real codebase. Evidence: no project tree copy occurs; only basename(target_path) is written into tmpdir; test_cmd is executed from tmpdir without source tree replication.
FOLLOW: Downstream, fix evaluation verdicts become silently wrong. A safe fix can be marked HARMFUL because isolated analysis sees import/module failures unrelated to the fix. A harmful fix can also be mis-scored if whole-project interactions are not exercised. This crosses the interface into immune_agents.py Stage 4, where SAFE/NEUTRAL results set `finding.verified = True`; if endocrine verdicts are ungrounded, the bug-closed gate can close or refuse to close bugs incorrectly, directly affecting dedup, escalation, and convergence behaviour.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — create a sandbox copy of the relevant source tree rooted at the common parent of `source_paths`, patch the target file at its relative path inside that copied tree, and run tools/tests against the sandboxed tree instead of a lone temp file.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.92
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — test execution in evaluate_fix() can validate the wrong code. The function runs `test_cmd` unchanged in `cwd=tmpdir`, but does not rewrite file arguments inside the command and does not ensure imports resolve to the patched sandbox. Example from immune_agents.py: `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`. In the tmpdir created by endocrine, `bench/tests/` does not exist, so tests either fail for environment reasons or run against the original installed/project code depending on invocation/import mechanics, not the patched file.
FOLLOW: This makes the “tests_passed” signal untrustworthy. A patched fix can be marked HARMFUL due to missing test paths, or SAFE because tests accidentally import original code rather than sandboxed code. That directly corrupts `FixEvaluation.verdict`, which immune_agents.py uses to mark fixes verified and close bugs. The feature “sandbox-test proposed fixes” therefore does not reliably fire end-to-end.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when creating the sandbox tree, rewrite or construct the test command to run against sandbox-relative paths within that tree, and set the subprocess cwd to the sandbox root so imports and test discovery target the patched sandbox.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41
DESCRIPTION: FIND — scan_health() reports tools as available even when the binary is missing. Each runner returns `[]` on `result.stderr == "NOT_FOUND"`, and scan_health() sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` whenever the runner returns without raising. Evidence: run_pyright/run_ruff/run_bandit/run_mypy all swallow NOT_FOUND into empty diagnostics; scan_health has no separate availability probe and treats successful function return as availability.
FOLLOW: Downstream health reports can claim the bench is healthy while analysis tools were never run. That is silently misleading to the human reviewer and to any insect-brain logic consuming `tools_available`. Missing pyright/ruff/bandit/mypy becomes indistinguishable from “zero findings”, so the health-scan feature can appear to fire cleanly when it is dead.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — have each tool runner return both diagnostics and an availability flag, or expose NOT_FOUND distinctly so scan_health() sets `tools_available[tool_name] = False` when the binary is absent.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.78
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.35
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the advertised defect-detection capability is not implemented as an exported function. endocrine.py claims core function 2 is “Defect detect — classify findings by defect category”, but the module only categorises raw tool diagnostics during scan_health via private helpers like `_categorise_pyright` and `_categorise_ruff`. There is no public defect-detection pass over findings or any integration in EndocrineLayer.run/report beyond health scan, fix evaluation, and pacing.
FOLLOW: This leaves a documented feature dead from the coordinator interface. Insect-brain or future callers cannot invoke a separate defect-detection stage for findings, and reviewers relying on endocrine’s advertised four functions will not see function 2 fire. For a PoC, dead advertised features are high risk if they are expected in the human review demo.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — add a minimal public defect-detection function that maps `HealthScan.diagnostics` into category counts/findings and include its output in EndocrineReport, or remove the claim from the module/docstrings if that feature is intentionally not shipped in this PoC.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.71
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44
DESCRIPTION: FIND — health_trend() produces ragged/incomplete time series that omit zero-count rounds. It only appends counts for categories present in each scan: `for cat, count in scan.counts_by_category.items(): trend.setdefault(cat, []).append(count)`. If a category disappears in a later round, no 0 is appended; if it appears late, earlier rounds are missing entirely.
FOLLOW: Downstream trend consumers cannot align series by round index reliably. A category going from 3 to 0 findings looks like a shorter list instead of improvement to zero. This can mislead any pacing or review logic that depends on worsening/improving code health over rounds and makes the history structurally inconsistent.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — build the union of seen categories across scan history and emit one count per round for every category, filling absent rounds with 0.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006
SEVERITY: 0.63
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.29
DESCRIPTION: FIND — slow-model and response-size anomaly detection use the upper median element instead of the statistical median for even-sized model sets. In compute_pacing_signals(), median is computed as `sorted(vals)[len(vals) // 2]`. With 4 or 6 models this picks the higher middle value, inflating the threshold and suppressing alerts.
FOLLOW: Pacing signals can fail to fire when one model is materially slower/larger than peers, especially in the 5-model environment if one entry is missing/zero-filtered and the effective sample becomes even. That degrades the inter-round pacing feedback the insect brain uses for timeout/degrade decisions.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — compute the true median, e.g. with `statistics.median`, for both duration and response_chars thresholds.
VERIFIED: TRUE
